title: CORS Errors Explained Simply
intro: Seen "blocked by CORS policy" in your console? Here's what's actually happening and how to fix it.

slides.heading: Same-origin policy
slides.subtitle: The browser's default rule.
points: Pages can't read responses from other origins by default
It protects users from malicious sites

slides.heading: What CORS is
slides.subtitle: A way for servers to opt in.
points: The browser checks it before sharing the response
The server decides, not the frontend

slides.heading: Preflight requests
slides.subtitle: The browser asks first.
points: An OPTIONS request sent before some requests
Triggered by methods like PUT or custom headers
The server must reply with what it allows

slides.heading: How to fix it
slides.subtitle: Fix it on the server.
points: Allow specific origins, especially with cookies
Use a dev-server proxy during local development

scenario.situation: Your React app on localhost:5173 calls your API on localhost:3000.
scenario.problem: The browser blocks the response with a CORS error, even though the same request works in Postman.
scenario.fix: Allow that origin on the API, for example in Express: app.use(cors({ origin: "http://localhost:5173" })).
scenario.takeaway: CORS is fixed on the server, not the frontend.
